title: الفصل الرابع عشر من الباب الرابع في صفة قلم الحكيم سيوريانوس الذي الف كتب الفلك . واسرار النجوم . والطلسمات وخواصها . والرصد . وعمل خواتيم الكواكب . وتسخير روحانياتها وجلبها — Hammer: "SECTION XIV. The alphabet of Syourianos the philosopher, (v. orig. p. 36.) He wrote in this alphabet on astronomy, … on the effects of planet-rings; and on the invocation and conjuration of spirits." [Chapter IV, English p. 7]

table: The pen of the sage Siyūriyānūs (سيوريانوس; Hammer: "Syourianos"). In this file's own paraphrase of the Arabic heading, he wrote books on the sphere, the secrets of the stars, talismans and their properties, al-raṣd (الرصد; Hammer: "magic alarm-posts"), the making of the seals of the planets (عمل خواتيم الكواكب; Hammer: "the effects of planet-rings") and the subjection and drawing down of their spirits (Hammer: "the invocation and conjuration of spirits"). These are the heading's claims about him; the seals of the planets it names are not identified here with any other set of seals. 28 signs in four rows (9, 8, 7, 4), read right to left, each with an Arabic letter printed beneath it, in abjad order from ا to غ; every label was read from the scan and agrees with that order.
conventions: Centre-line strokes with the kit pen (5.5), a little heavier than the print's line (about 3.5-4.5 units). The ring-ends are kit rings, one for each closed ring the print shows, with r set to the centre line of the printed ring (3.5-6.2); the stroke stops at the ring's edge, and the ring is placed where the print has it, even where it sits beside the line of the stroke rather than on it. Many printed rings are ovals, flat or tall, and some are loops the stroke makes by crossing itself; all are drawn as the kit's round rings, centred on the printed ring. Curls that turn round but leave a gap (no enclosed paper in the scan) are drawn as open curls, not rings. Small closed triangles at stroke ends are drawn as closed triangle paths. A loop through which the stroke runs on (bāʾ) is part of the path, not a ring. Separator points between the signs are not part of any sign. Exception (added by the independent checker): the closed triangle at the end of bāʾ is drawn about a third larger than printed so that its opening, plain in all three copies, does not fill in at the kit's pen weight; the smaller triangular heads of kāf, qāf, shīn and thāʾ, whose openings are only specks, are drawn at their printed size and read as solid.

letters.name: alif
letters.strokes: An upright stroke ending at each end in a ring set to its left: a small, tightly closed ring at the top, a larger one at the foot.
letters.note: The top ring is printed almost filled in (its opening is a speck); it is drawn as an open ring.

letters.name: bāʾ
letters.strokes: One stroke: a short tail at the lower left rises into a closed loop standing on the line, runs on to the right as a long level stroke and ends in a small closed triangle, point upward.
letters.note: The figure at the right end is printed as a small closed triangle, point upward, rather than a round ring; it is drawn as a triangle, about a third larger than printed so that its opening (plain in all three copies) does not fill in at the kit's pen weight. The loop at the left is part of the stroke (the line runs through its foot), not a ring at an end.

letters.strokes: Two legs spreading down from the outer lower corners of a pair of small rings side by side at the top, the left leg ending in a ring, the right one in an open curl; a sagging stroke crosses both, from a ring at the upper left to a ring at the right.
letters.note: The top is a tangle at the scale of the print (about 15 by 9 units): two small loops sharing a wall, with a short stroke inside the right loop running from the shared wall down to its lower right, the same in all three copies. It is drawn as two touching rings, one on each leg; the inner stroke is not drawn, because at the kit's pen weight it would fill the ring. The curl at the foot of the right leg does not close in any copy and is drawn open.

letters.name: dhāl
letters.strokes: Two interlaced chevrons, a > and a <, each running from a ring at the top to a ring at the bottom; they cross twice, enclosing a lozenge between them.
letters.note: The four rings are printed as flat ovals; they are drawn round, centred on the printed rings. The upper arm of the > bows: it leaves its ring steeply and flattens after the first crossing.

letters.name: ḍād
letters.strokes: An inverted V from a high peak, its feet ending in rings at the lower left and lower right, interlaced with a Y: a V from a ring at the upper left and an open curl at the upper right, meeting in a stem that runs down below the figure.
letters.note: This is the most tangled sign of the table. The ambiguous details are the crossings of the two figures, read as an inverted V laid over a Y, and the upper-right curl, which turns round but leaves a gap in the Wellcome and Getty copies (it closes in the UNC copy); it is drawn open, its end kept clear of the stroke so that the gap shows at the kit's pen weight. In the Wellcome scan the lower-left ring also touches the central stem, closing a small eye between them (about x 41-46, y 48-56); the Getty and UNC copies show no such eye, and the ring is drawn a little apart from the stem.

letters.note: The ambiguous details are the crossings of the two figures, read as an inverted V laid over a V, and the lower-left curl, which does not close in the print and is drawn open.
